title: Slow-Cooker Beef Stew
subtitle: Rich slow-cooked stew with root vegetables and dumplings
excerpt: Chunks of beef chuck browned and then cooked in a slow cooker for 8 hours with carrots, potatoes, and a deep beef and ale broth. Suet dumplings added in the final 45 minutes. Minimal effort, maximum depth.

recipe.sourceNotes: Slow-cooker beef stew converts tough, inexpensive cuts (chuck, shin, cheek) into tender, falling-apart meat through collagen-to-gelatin conversion at low temperature over many hours. The key rule of slow-cooker stew is to brown the meat first: the slow cooker cannot develop the Maillard reaction flavours that browning produces. The browning step takes 15 minutes and makes a significant difference to the finished depth of flavour.

content.text: Brown the beef in a hot pan before it goes into the slow cooker: this step builds the flavour base. Do not crowd the pan or the meat will steam instead of brown. Work in two or three batches. The suet dumplings go on top of the stew for the final 45 minutes with the lid on.

Season the beef chunks with salt and pepper. Dust lightly with the plain flour. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Brown the beef in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per batch, turning to colour all sides. Transfer to the slow cooker.

Reduce the heat to medium. Cook the onion in the same pan for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato puree. Cook for 1 minute. Pour in the beer and scrape up any browned bits. Pour this over the beef in the slow cooker.
Add the carrots, potato, Worcestershire sauce, beef stock, bay leaves, and thyme. Stir briefly. Cook on LOW for 7 to 8 hours or HIGH for 4 to 5 hours.

For dumplings: mix the self-raising flour and suet with a pinch of salt. Add enough cold water to make a soft, slightly sticky dough (about 6 to 8 tablespoons). Shape into 10 small balls. Place on top of the stew 45 minutes before serving. Replace the lid and cook on HIGH for 45 minutes until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through.
